Statistical Decision Guidance

Source: R/stats.R
statistical_decision.Rd

Selects recommended statistical methods based on sample size and the degree of censoring.

Usage

statistical_decision(
  percent_censored,
  n_used,
  n_detect,
  profile = guidance_profile("epa_unified")
)

Arguments

percent_censored

Numeric percentage of censored observations.

n_used

Number of non-missing observations available for statistical evaluation.

n_detect

Number of detected (non-censored) observations.

profile

A guidance profile created by [guidance_profile()].

Value

A tibble with class `"statistical_decision"`.

The returned object contains:

n_used

Number of analytical results used in evaluation.

n_detect

Number of uncensored observations.

percent_censored

Percentage of observations classified as censored.

censoring_class

Censoring category: `"low_censoring"`, `"moderate_censoring"`, `"high_censoring"`, or `"extreme_censoring"`.

distribution_method

Recommended distributional analysis approach.

trend_method

Recommended trend evaluation method.

trend_guidance

Recommended interpretation of trend results.

censored_method

Recommended censored-data treatment method for trend analyses.

distribution_config

Configuration list suitable for [estimate_distribution()].

interval_config

Configuration list suitable for interval estimation functions.

decision_basis

Primary basis for the recommendation.

Details

This function implements a rule-based statistical decision framework for environmental monitoring data. Recommendations are based on the percentage of censored observations and the number of observations available for evaluation.

Returned guidance can be used to select:

  • distribution estimation methods

  • trend analysis approaches

  • censored-data handling methods

  • interval estimation settings

The default profile follows EPA-style guidance in which parametric methods are preferred for low censoring, regression-on-order statistics (ROS) is preferred for moderate censoring, and nonparametric methods are preferred when censoring becomes extensive.

Distribution recommendations are assigned as follows:

ConditionRecommendationMethod
n_used < 4insufficient_datano distribution fit
low censoringparametricnormal/lognormal evaluation
moderate censoringros_censoredcensored distribution fitting
high censoringnonparametricnonparametric methods
extreme censoringdescriptive_onlydescriptive summaries only

Trend recommendations always use a Mann-Kendall framework, although interpretation guidance may recommend screening-level evaluation when censoring is extensive.

See also

[derive_decision()], [estimate_distribution()], [guidance_profile()], [guidance_options()]

Examples

statistical_decision(
  percent_censored = 12,
  n_used = 20,
  n_detect = 18
)
#> <statistical_decision>
#>   n_used n_detect percent_censored censoring_class distribution_method
#> 1     20       18               12   low_censoring          parametric
#>   trend_method    trend_guidance censored_method distribution_config
#> 1 mann_kendall formal_trend_test     as_reported     sf, norm, lnorm
#>          interval_config decision_basis
#> 1 0.95, Bonferroni, 1, 1  low_censoring

statistical_decision(
  percent_censored = 75,
  n_used = 16,
  n_detect = 4
)
#> <statistical_decision>
#>   n_used n_detect percent_censored censoring_class distribution_method
#> 1     16        4               75  high_censoring       nonparametric
#>   trend_method    trend_guidance censored_method distribution_config
#> 1 mann_kendall formal_trend_test          cenken     sf, norm, lnorm
#>          interval_config decision_basis
#> 1 0.95, Bonferroni, 1, 1 high_censoring

statistical_decision(
  percent_censored = c(5, 25, 80),
  n_used = c(10, 10, 10),
  n_detect = c(9, 7, 2)
)
#> <statistical_decision>
#>   n_used n_detect percent_censored    censoring_class distribution_method
#> 1     10        9                5      low_censoring          parametric
#> 2     10        7               25 moderate_censoring        ros_censored
#> 3     10        2               80     high_censoring       nonparametric
#>   trend_method       trend_guidance censored_method distribution_config
#> 1 mann_kendall    formal_trend_test     as_reported     sf, norm, lnorm
#> 2 mann_kendall    formal_trend_test          cenken     sf, norm, lnorm
#> 3 mann_kendall insufficient_detects          cenken     sf, norm, lnorm
#>          interval_config     decision_basis
#> 1 0.95, Bonferroni, 1, 1      low_censoring
#> 2 0.95, Bonferroni, 1, 1 moderate_censoring
#> 3 0.95, Bonferroni, 1, 1     high_censoring
